title: Controlled failover test matrix (SRE) — Regional failover automation upgrade
content:
Working assumptions (update if trigger policy changes)
- Regions used in tests: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2 (target) unless otherwise specified.
- Traffic slices:
  - “canary” = internal + low-risk hosted routes + tier=dev (no enterprise) unless explicitly noted.
  - Progressive failover stages: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (per route + tier scoping).
- Trigger windows (initial): 5m evaluation window, 15m sustain requirement for “FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED”, 20m hold-down after failover/rollback.
- Hysteresis (initial): require 2 consecutive windows to transition into FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS; require 3 consecutive “healthy” windows to transition back to HEALTHY.
- Safe-to-failover gates (must be TRUE to automate):
  - target_region_gpu_headroom_pct >= 30% (and not trending down faster than -5%/5m)
  - target_region_queue_depth < threshold (per route class)
  - dependency_health(target) = green for auth, routing policy store, token accounting, key-value cache (where applicable)
  - routing_policy_sanity_check passes (no circular routes; canary policies present)
- Stop conditions are hard stops: abort + rollback to baseline routing if any stop condition is hit.

Legend
- Signals:
  - app_5xx_rate, app_timeout_rate
  - p50/p95/p99_latency_ms
  - edge_5xx_rate / edge_timeout_rate
  - net_packet_loss_pct, net_rtt_ms (synthetic probes)
  - capacity_gpu_util_pct, queue_depth, queue_wait_ms
  - dependency_error_rate (policy store, auth, KMS)
- Expected states (orchestrator): HEALTHY, DEGRADED (no failover), FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED, FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS, FAILED_OVER, ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS
- “Action” describes automation intent; if running in monitor-only mode, we should still observe expected state recommendations + audit logs.

Spreadsheet-style matrix
| ID | Scenario | Impairment method (how we simulate) | Expected signals / thresholds crossed | Expected trigger outcome | Expected orchestration action | Progressive scope | Safe-to-failover expected | Stop conditions (abort/rollback) | Verification steps (what to check) | Notes / owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CF-01 | Elevated 5xx (app) in primary | Inject 5xx in model gateway for us-east-1 only (e.g., fault injection in staging; in prod use canary route w/ controlled error) | app_5xx_rate > 2% for 5m; burn-rate alert candidate; p99 may spike | DEGRADED -> FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED within 10–20m (depending on sustain) | Move canary slice away from primary; if persists and gates pass, proceed to FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS | Canary (5% of hosted chat route) | TRUE (target headroom ok; deps green) | Target region app_5xx_rate > 1%; p99 target > 2x baseline; SLO burn > 2x expected; unexpected enterprise traffic included | 1) Confirm audit log “reason=app_5xx_rate” 2) Routing distribution shifts by % 3) Impact: 5xx drops for canary cohort 4) No spillover to non-scoped routes | Miles / Mina: confirm routing policy scoping works as intended |
| CF-02 | Elevated timeouts (queue) due to saturation in primary | Limit concurrency / artificially reduce worker pool capacity in us-east-1 | queue_depth rising; queue_wait_ms > threshold; app_timeout_rate > 0.5% | DEGRADED; may produce FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED if sustained | Prefer graceful degradation first (load shed + tightened timeouts), then progressive failover if still burning | Canary -> 25% on embeddings route only | TRUE if target has headroom | Load shed triggers for wrong tier; target queue_depth spikes; token accounting lag > 2m | 1) Confirm graceful degradation flags engaged before failover 2) queue_depth stabilizes 3) canary failover reduces timeouts 4) ensure no flappy oscillation | Rafael: ensure “degrade-before-failover” ordering is respected for saturation |
| CF-03 | Tail latency regression (no large 5xx) | Introduce latency injection (e.g., sleep) in primary inference scheduler for subset of models | p99_latency_ms > 2x baseline for 10m; 5xx remains < 1% | DEGRADED (no automatic failover if policy requires multi-signal) OR FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED if tail-only triggers enabled for tier=enterprise | If configured: progressive failover for impacted model(s) only; otherwise remain DEGRADED + recommend manual review | Model-scoped: model=rx-llama-70b-vX only | TRUE | If failover: target p99 also degrades; if no failover: customer-visible p99 > SLO for > 20m | 1) Verify trigger policy for tail-only conditions 2) Confirm model-scoped routing works 3) Compare p99 per model per region 4) Verify no unrelated models moved | Aisha: align with latency SLO policy to avoid “failover on noise” |
| CF-04 | Partial network packet loss to primary edge | Apply tc/netem packet loss on a subset of edge->primary links OR simulate by dropping probe traffic (staging) | net_packet_loss_pct > 3% and probe failure rate > threshold; edge_timeout_rate rises | FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED (network) | If safe gates pass: route canary traffic to target region; confirm edge routing updates | Canary -> 25% on streaming chat | TRUE if target path healthy | Cross-region RTT spikes > 2x; streaming disconnects increase in target; DNS propagation anomalies | 1) Probe dashboards show impairment 2) Failover decision cites probes 3) Streaming disconnect rate improves 4) Confirm TTL/edge routing changed as expected | Victor: ensure probe placement avoids false positives |
| CF-05 | Upstream dependency failure in primary (policy store) | Fail requests from primary to routing policy store / simulate 500s | dependency_error_rate(policy_store) > 5%; app_5xx_rate rises secondarily | FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED only if dependency is region-scoped and target is healthy | If dependency is truly regional: fail over scoped routes; otherwise hold (avoid moving into shared failure) | Hosted routes using dynamic policies | TRUE only if dependency health(target)=green | Dependency error also present in target; auth errors emerge; audit shows “shared dependency” but still fails over | 1) Confirm safe-to-failover blocks when dependency is shared 2) Orchestrator remains DEGRADED w/ “unsafe to failover” reason 3) Incident bot message includes gating reason | Ethan: validate dependency classification (regional vs global) is correctly encoded |
| CF-06 | DNS/edge routing misconfiguration (negative test) | Introduce invalid routing policy config in staging | routing_policy_sanity_check fails | Should NOT fail over; should page/alert on config sanity only | No orchestration action; remain HEALTHY/DEGRADED depending on impact | N/A | FALSE (sanity gate blocks) | Any automation changes applied despite sanity failure | 1) Confirm orchestrator refuses action 2) Audit shows “blocked: sanity_check” 3) Runbook steps to fix config referenced | Connor: use as release-gating validation before prod flag enable |
| CF-07 | Target region insufficient capacity (safety gate) | Artificially mark target headroom low (or drain target fleet in staging) while primary impaired | capacity_gpu_headroom_pct(target) < 30%; queue_depth rising in target | FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED may occur, but should remain “blocked” | No automatic failover; recommend manual mitigation (load shed / throttle) | Canary only (recommendation) | FALSE | Failover proceeds anyway; target overload causes wider outage | 1) Confirm “blocked by capacity” reason in audit + incident bot 2) Confirm load shed policy kicks in for protected tiers 3) Confirm no DNS/edge change occurs | Harish: confirm authoritative capacity signals + refresh intervals |
| CF-08 | Flappy signals (false-positive resistance) | Oscillate 5xx between 0.5% and 2.5% every 3–4 minutes | app_5xx_rate crosses threshold but not sustained | Should stay DEGRADED at most; no FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS due to hysteresis | No orchestration action | N/A | TRUE (but should still not act) | Any failover action taken; repeated state churn; pages > expected | 1) Verify state machine does not transition to FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS 2) Check hold-down timer behavior 3) Alert noise: only warning, no page | Sergio/Aisha: use to tune alerting + hysteresis parameters |
| CF-09 | Multi-signal severe outage in primary | Combine 5xx + timeouts + probe failures in primary | app_5xx_rate > 5% + timeout_rate > 1% + probes failing > threshold | Fast FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED and, if gates pass, FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS | Progressive failover quickly escalates (5% -> 25% -> 50%), stop before 100% unless explicitly approved | Tier-scoped: dev + growth only | TRUE | Any enterprise tier inadvertently included; target region degradation; error budget burn in target | 1) Confirm correct tier scoping 2) Confirm stage timing aligns with runbook 3) Confirm recovery in customer-impact metrics 4) Confirm audit entries per stage | Rafael (IC scenario): this is the “happy path” severe failure |
| CF-10 | Rollback test (post failover recovery) | After CF-09, remove impairment and hold healthy for required windows | Signals recover; probes pass; 5xx/timeouts return to baseline | Transition to ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS then HEALTHY after hold-down and healthy windows | Rollback progressive stages (50% -> 25% -> 5% -> baseline) | Same scope as failover | TRUE | Rollback causes re-degradation; flaps between regions; traffic pinned incorrectly | 1) Verify rollback honors hold-down timer 2) Confirm routing returns to baseline 3) Confirm no lingering edge records / stale policies 4) Verify post-rollback SLO stable | Miles: ensure rollback semantics mirror failover semantics |
| CF-11 | Graceful degradation without failover (regional impairment) | Induce moderate impairment: p99 + mild 5xx but below failover threshold | DEGRADED triggers; load shed for low tiers; fallback model variants used | Should remain DEGRADED (no failover) | Engage load shedding + tighter timeouts + model variant fallback per policy | Tier-scoped behavior (free/dev see shed first) | N/A | Protected tiers throttled unexpectedly; fallback model violates allowlist; quality regression alarms | 1) Verify correct shed order by tier 2) Confirm fallback model selection matches allowlist 3) Confirm request success improves 4) Confirm quality monitoring doesn’t flag major regression | Mina/Marissa: ensure tier protections and fallback policy are consistent |
| CF-12 | Streaming-specific impairment | Inject streaming disconnects (RST) at edge for primary region only | streaming_disconnect_rate increases; may not show 5xx | If streaming signal included: FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED for streaming routes only; otherwise DEGRADED + manual action suggested | Progressive failover for streaming endpoints only | Route-scoped: /v1/chat/completions?stream=true | TRUE | Non-streaming endpoints moved; target streaming also unstable | 1) Confirm route scoping works 2) Compare streaming disconnect rates pre/post 3) Confirm non-streaming unaffected | Victor + SRE: this matches prior SUP-19312 symptoms |
| CF-13 | Dedicated customer scoped failover (enterprise constraints) | In staging dedicated slice, impair primary region for dedicated pool | dedicated_pool_error_rate > threshold; capacity constraints visible | FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED; require explicit approval if enterprise | Failover only that customer’s pool/tenant | Customer-scoped | TRUE if target dedicated pool headroom ok | Any cross-tenant impact; isolation breached; customer traffic leaks to hosted pool | 1) Verify tenant isolation 2) Verify scoping labels in routing policy 3) Confirm audit trail references customer_id 4) Confirm support macro correctness | Dev Patel: ensure support + comms expectations align |
| CF-14 | Monitor-only mode validation (no changes) | Run CF-01 style impairment but keep automation disabled | Signals cross thresholds; state transitions logged | FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED emitted; no DNS/edge/routing changes applied | No action (monitor-only) | Canary | TRUE | Any real routing change despite monitor-only | 1) Confirm “monitor-only” guardrail enforced 2) Incident bot posts recommendation + linkouts 3) Verify no routing policy diff | Connor: required before enabling prod flags |
| CF-15 | Cross-region dependency regression (target unhealthy) | Impair target-only dependency (e.g., auth latency) while primary also mildly impaired | dependency_health(target)=yellow/red; primary DEGRADED | Should remain blocked; no failover to bad target | No action; recommend mitigation in primary | N/A | FALSE | Automation fails over anyway; worsens impact | 1) Confirm gating blocks 2) Audit cites target dependency 3) Verify alerting correctly indicates “no safe target” state | Ethan + Irene: validate dependency gating is authoritative |
| CF-16 | DNS TTL / propagation risk check | Execute edge record change in a sandbox domain; measure propagation by region/ISP | TTL observed; propagation delays; residual traffic to old region | Not a trigger test; change-management validation | No orchestrator involvement; infra-only | N/A | N/A | Long tail traffic sticks to old region beyond expected; rollback slow | 1) Measure % traffic still on old target after T+5, T+10, T+20 2) Validate rollback time 3) Document in runbook | Victor + Connor: feed into controlled prod window planning |

Per-test “definition of done” checklist (quick)
- Audit log has: signals snapshot + thresholds + gating result + human override metadata (if any)
- Routing distribution matches intended progressive stage within expected convergence time
- SLO dashboard: customer-visible 5xx/timeout/p99 improves for scoped cohort; no meaningful regression outside scope
- Capacity: target remains within headroom guardrails; no runaway queue depth
- Alerts: expected pages fire (only when intended); no excess noise; alert links point to runbook/dashboard
- Runbook updates: any discovered ambiguity gets captured (owner + due date)

Open questions / TODO (as of last edit)
- Do we treat p99-only regressions for enterprise as sufficient for FAILOVER_RECOMMENDED, or require multi-signal confirmation?
- Finalize thresholds per route class (streaming vs non-streaming; chat vs embeddings) to avoid false positives.
- Confirm which probe locations are “authoritative” vs advisory to avoid triggering off a single bad vantage point.
- Document expected DNS/edge convergence distributions (p50/p95) for prod.
